item.subject: science
item.stem: Meena left a bowl of cooked dal uncovered on the kitchen counter, and by the next morning it had turned sour. Beside it, a jar of mango pickle made with plenty of salt and oil stayed fresh for many months. Which statement best explains why the dal rotted but the pickle did not get infected in the same way?

options.A: The dal rotted because it was naturally weak, while the pickle stayed safe simply because it is a pickle.
options.B: Microorganisms from the air and surroundings settled on the exposed dal and made it rot, while the high salt in the pickle acted as a preservative that prevented microbial infection.
options.C: The dal rotted first and the rotting itself produced the microorganisms that soured it.
options.D: Only a large amount of salt or sugar can stop microorganisms, so the small amount of salt in the pickle played no role in keeping it fresh.
